resources.string: Maintenance guidance, dashboard lights and common symptom guidance in one place.
Generic guidance based on mileage and your recorded services. Check your owner manual for the exact schedule.

Tap a light to understand what it can mean and the safest next step.
Low oil pressure can damage an engine very quickly. Stop in a safe place, switch the engine off and check the oil level. Do not keep driving if the warning remains on.
The engine may be overheating. Turn off heavy loads such as A/C, stop safely and let the engine cool. Never open a hot cooling system. Seek service if the warning persists.
This can indicate the parking brake, low brake fluid or a braking-system fault. If braking feels weak, the pedal changes suddenly or the warning stays red, stop safely and arrange inspection.
The charging system may not be supplying power correctly. Reduce unnecessary electrical loads and have the battery, alternator and belt checked before the vehicle loses electrical power.
A steady light usually means the engine-management system detected a fault. Arrange diagnosis soon. If it flashes, reduce load and stop driving if the engine runs roughly or power drops sharply.
Normal braking may remain available but anti-lock assistance can be disabled. Drive cautiously, increase following distance and arrange an inspection.
Choose a common symptom for possible causes and a sensible first check.
Common causes include low coolant, a leak, fan failure, thermostat trouble or a cooling-system fault. If the gauge enters the red zone or steam appears, stop safely and switch the engine off.

Possible causes include ignition misfire, dirty intake/throttle components, worn engine mounts, vacuum leaks or fuel-delivery issues. If the check-engine light flashes, avoid hard driving and inspect promptly.

Squealing can come from worn pads or contamination; grinding can mean severe pad wear. If braking performance changes, vibration is strong or grinding is persistent, inspect the brakes as soon as possible.
Noise when turning the steering wheel

Possible causes include steering or suspension joints, strut mounts, belt-driven power steering components on some cars, or low steering fluid where applicable. Inspect sooner if steering becomes heavy or loose.

Check tire pressure, recent driving pattern, air filter condition, maintenance history and whether a warning light is present. A persistent increase can also come from sensors, ignition or fuel-system problems.

Rovena provides general guidance from the information you enter. It cannot inspect the vehicle or replace the manufacturer schedule, a diagnostic scan or a qualified mechanic. Safety-critical symptoms should be checked professionally.
